title: Orphan claim conversion: Link policy completes the claim (details, location, coverages, reserves, parties, loss event)
walkthroughSteps: Every case starts on a skeleton claim's Claim Overview; the Link policy sheet is one sheet with four steps (Policy, Claim details, Coverages, Reserves).
Reset in the DEV bar puts all skeleton claims back.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · Storm skeleton keeps a cause the lookup knows
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-004 (storm damage, one policy to choose from).

**You see:** Step 2 *Complete the claim*: the loss description is filled in and required; **Cause of loss = Natural Event** (storm is read as a Natural Event), no note. The progress tracker on the left shows Policy ✓, Claim details, Coverages, Reserves.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-001), then Next: *Choose the coverages*. Tick a location, Next, optionally enter a reserve (a sub-type is required once an amount is entered), then **Link policy** and confirm. The overview shows **Natural Event**, a loss event ID, and the new claim number.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · Business interruption asks the CBI questions
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-008 (business interruption, supplier fire).

**You see:** Step 2 shows **Cause of loss = Business Interruption** and the CBI box (the same one FNOL shows): the question, then case type, supplier name and originating location. Required fields carry a *.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-005). Press Next with *Yes* and nothing else: it is blocked. Choose *Supplier — Named*, enter a name and a location, or answer *No*, then continue; coverages offer a Business interruption entity as well as the building.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · No cause on the skeleton becomes Other Event and still gets a section
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-009 (damage reported, cause still unclear).

**You see:** Step 2 shows **Cause of loss = Other Event** with the note "The skeleton claim has no cause of loss, so it was set to Other Event. You can change it." and an optional *Specify other cause*.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-006), Next, tick the coverage, Next, **Link policy**. The converted claim has the cause Other Event and one section (never 0).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · No location on the skeleton: adding one is optional
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-010 (storm damage, no location typed at creation).

**You see:** Step 2 *Location of loss*: "No location was entered on the skeleton claim. You can add one now, or later via Edit claim details." with an optional **Add location** button.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-007). Press Add location to open the policy + manual sheet, pick one: it shows with *Change* / *Remove*. Or skip it and continue.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · Location is kept unless the handler changes it; no nearby policy location
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-006 (water damage, typed address in Munich; the policy's locations are in Berlin and Dresden).

**You see:** Step 2 shows the typed address as a manual location with **Keep this location** (selected) / **Change location**. Nothing opens by itself.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-003). Press *Change location*: the sheet says none of the policy's locations is in the same city or postal code, with nothing pre-selected. Cancel returns to Keep; picking one shows *Change again* / *Use the skeleton location*.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy · Coverages, reserves, parties and loss event are built at conversion
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Claim Overview of SK-2024-005 (fire, exact policy location match).

**You see:** After Link policy: the claim number changes (the SK number stays as an alias), the sections are the ticked coverages, reserves entered in the sheet are Pending on the Reserves page, **the insured and broker are on the claim** (Make Payment's payee list), and the overview shows a **Loss event ID** that opens its own page.

**Try:** Press **Link policy**, choose the policy on the list (POL-2026-002), Next, tick one coverage, Next, enter a reserve and a sub-type, **Link policy**, confirm. Check Sections, Reserves, Make Payment's Payee dropdown and the Loss event ID link.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: All claims · Skeletons are flagged and filterable
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** All claims.

**You see:** Skeleton rows show an **Awaiting policy** chip beside Open. The Status filter offers *Awaiting policy*, which lists only those claims.

**Try:** Choose *Awaiting policy* in Status and press Filter: 8 claims, all SK-. After linking one, it leaves the list.
